newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes firmer at day's high in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes firmer at day's high in Hong Kong.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed firmer at the day's high on Friday after trading within a 40 U.S. cent range all day in an extremely quiet session, dealers said.
"The yellow metal was pushed up by the U.S. dollar dips," said a dealer at a major bank. "But the market is going to remain range-bound between US$340 and $345."
Bullion ended at US$344.40/90 an ounce, up from New York's US$343.50/344.00 close on Thursday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$342.40/90.
"Players are unsure of where the market is turning next and most dealers are watching U.S. dollar movements in the short term," another dealer said.
Local gold ended HK$18 higher at HK$3,185 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -6.00 from its previous fix at -6.50.
